Applicant is in detention since 12.03.2023.

sentences.text: Prosecutrix was recovered after some time and in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she stated that on 04.01.2023 two boys met her and they asked to give number of her friend.

She also received a call from Raju Singh R/o Anuppur and he asked her to reach at Bilaspur, she went to Bilaspur and from there proceeded for Raipur and in Raipur she met with Raju who attempted to commit rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
Thereafter, he dropped her near a home.
She was dropped at Bilaspur Railway Station by one biker.
She came into contact with one boy named Rahul and remained with him for two days.
One boy named Dwivedi made a call and asked her to reach Pendra but when she reached Pendra, Dwivedi was not there.

Therefore,
she proceeded for Budhar and stayed with her friend Abhishek.
Dwivedi again made a call to her and met her at Bijuri Railway Station and took her in a room and attempted to commit rape upon her and dropped her at Bijuri Railway Station.
Thereafter, two boys who were having masked faces took her to jungle side and slapped her.
When they were taking her to throw in the river, she screamed and hearing her scream, one woman reached there, at this, they fled away from there.
FIR was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
4 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50881 3 MCRC-42165-2024
He is in jail since 12.03.2023 i.e. almost a period of more than 18 months and in this case, prosecutrix has not been examined.
It is contended that prosecutrix is not traceable and trial Court has issued arrest warrant against her to procure her appearance for deposition.
It is submitted that there is no allegation of rape against him.
As prosecutrix is untraceable and even police is not able to trace her

, therefore,
trial of the case will take time.
It is further submitted that co-accused Anand Kumar Sahu has already been released on bail vide order dated 18.09.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.28786 of 2024.
Hence, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
5 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.

6 . Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, detention period of the applicant and the fact that prosecutrix is untraceable despite issuance of arrest warrant by the trial Court, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this second bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C., 1973 (Section 483 of BNSS, 2023) for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

7 . It is directed that applicant - Prem Singh Yadav be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties each of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:50881 4 MCRC-42165-2024 trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C., 1973 [Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023].
